title: Settlement and T+1
text: A trade is agreed in microseconds, but it is not finished. Shares still have to move one way and cash the other. In the US, since 28 May 2024, that happens one business day after the trade: T plus 1.

title: Why it matters
text: Every day between trade and settlement is a day a counterparty could fail, and a day the clearing house holds margin against it. The SEC set a three day cycle in 1993, replacing five business days. It moved to two days in 2017. On 15 February 2023 it adopted T plus 1, and compliance began on 28 May 2024. As the SEC chair put it, time is money and time is risk.

title: From trade to settlement
text: Here is the path. On trade date, the trade executes, and the exchange reports it to the clearing house. For institutional trades, brokers must get allocations, confirmations and affirmations done as soon as possible, and by the end of that same day. Overnight, the clearing house nets each member's trades in each stock down to one obligation. On T plus 1, shares and cash change hands, delivery against payment, so neither moves without the other.

title: Worked example
text: Count business days, not calendar days. Sell on a Monday, and you settle on Tuesday. Sell on a Friday, and you settle on Monday. Sell on Thursday, 3 July 2025, and Friday is the Independence Day holiday, so you settle on Monday, 7 July. Under the old T plus 2, that same trade would have settled on Tuesday, 8 July. One day shorter means one day less exposure, and less margin held against it.

title: Beyond the US
text: Shorter cycles squeeze the back office. Allocations, confirmations, securities lending recalls and currency funding all have less time. Not every market has moved yet. In the EU, Regulation 2025/2075 brings T plus 1 from 11 October 2027. Until then, a firm trading both sides of the Atlantic runs two settlement cycles at once.

title: In the lab
text: The lab stops at trade date, but it produces what settlement needs. The drop copy lists every firm execution, with a match number and a price in four-decimal fixed point. The research tools roll those fills up into net shares and net cash per symbol. Those two numbers per symbol are exactly what a firm would owe or receive on T plus 1.

title: Takeaway
text: So what do pros do? They confirm and affirm trades on the same day, by machine. They keep the holiday calendar in code, for every market they trade. They check stock is available before they sell it. And they plan funding for each settlement date, not each trade date. This is education, not legal advice.
